title: Minichain SDK: evented onramp + instrumented runbook (proposal)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact proposal for a tiny, event-driven SDK (Minichain) intended for rapid adoption by internal integrators and early external partners. Goal is to provide a zero-friction path from local prototype -> sandbox -> instrumented pilot (10k tokens/day) with baked-in telemetry and failure-mode guidance so product teams can evaluate Redwood behavior in realistic loops (prefix caching, kv-cache warmup, batching).

Problem statement:
- Current SDK docs are long and optimized for full-featured clients; they assume token-budget comfort and focus on embedding + generation.
- Integrators building conversational UIs or tool-bridges need a small, opinionated SDK that:
  * wires into event loops (websocket/edge functions)
  * exposes lightweight hooks for telemetry and deterministic warmups
  * is easy to polyglot-install (go/rust/python/js minimal surface)
- Without a compact onramp, teams copy-paste internal patterns and reintroduce costly batching anti-patterns or mis-instrument telemetry.

Proposal summary (what Minichain is):
- A ~1–2 file reference SDK (per language) that:
  * sends events (request.start, token.chunk, request.end, fallback.trigger) to Redwood and local telemetry sinks
  * provides a tiny policy layer for routing (hosted/dedicated/private) using attributes, so sample apps show graceful degradation to cheaper model variants
  * includes a warmup recipe for KV cache priming and a prefetch helper for expected prefixes
  * ships with a single-page quickstart doc + two runnable examples (chat widget and long-form assistant)

Success metrics (30/60/90 days):
- 30d: internal pilot (3 teams) can integrate Minichain skeleton and run 1k sample requests each; qualitative feedback logged
- 60d: one external beta partner runs the SDK in a sandbox (10k tokens/day) and we see telemetry for prefix cache hit-rate and token latency
- 90d: publish stable quickstart and lift at least 2 internal examples to official examples repo; reduce time-to-first-success (internal metric) from ~3 days to <4 hours for a sample app

Core components and API surface (sketch):
- EventEmitter (core):
  * on('request.start', metadata) => called before request sent
  * on('token', {delta, token_idx}) => streaming tokens as they arrive
  * on('request.end', {status, tokens, duration}) => finalizer
  * on('fallback', {reason, chosen_variant}) => when SDK triggers fallback rules
- Policy config (declarative JSON):
  * prefer: ["hosted", "dedicated:pool-42"]
  * failover: ["hosted:cheap-2", "hosted:latency-optim"]
  * qos: {latency_ms: 200, cost_per_1k: 0.003}
- Helpers:
  * kvWarm(primerText, model, timeoutMs) -> promise resolving when KV primed or timeout
  * batcher(minBatchSize, maxDelayMs) -> simple FIFO batch helper with backpressure hint
  * trace(spanName) -> minimal tracing stub that can attach to OpenTelemetry or console logs

Quickstart outline (developer flow):
1) Install: npm/pip/go get -> import Minichain
2) Wire a chat widget: const client = new Minichain({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, policy: 'default-sample'})
3) Attach events: client.on('token', t => appendToDom(t.delta))
4) Warm KV for user context: await client.kvWarm(userRecentMessages.slice(-3))
5) Demo fallback: flip policy to force cheap-variant and observe telemetry event 'fallback'

Instrumentation & telemetry contract (non-negotiable for this onramp):
- Minimum emitted events must include: request_id, model, variant, route_hint, request_ms, tokens_sent, tokens_received, kv_cache_hit_estimate, batch_size
- Events should be sent to both: local dev sink (stdout/console) and Redwood ingestion endpoint when running against sandbox accounts (toggle in config)
- Privacy note: do not send full user PII payloads; redaction helper included (default redaction for emails/SSNs)

Failure modes & recovery recipes (short):
- cold kv-cache => guide: run kvWarm with last-5-turns; if latency spike > 350ms for 3 consecutive reqs, send fallback event and route to cheaper model; show sample Slack alert rule
- sustained 429s => exponential backoff + progressive fallback to smaller batch sizes; sample policy json included
- streaming interruptions => client will buffer tokens for 500ms and attempt reconnect (idempotent request ids); doc explains limits

Example apps included:
- chat-widget-minichain: naive browser widget that streams tokens and shows fallback banner when fallback.trigger emitted
- nightly-summarizer: serverless function that batches conversations and demonstrates warmup + batcher usage (includes CI smoke test)

Rollout plan & milestones:
- Week 0–1: implement reference node/python minimal libs + two examples, internal demo to 3 integrator teams
- Week 2–3: instrument telemetry schema, add redaction & local-sink toggles, refine failure recipes from feedback
- Week 4: stabilize APIs, write final quickstart and one-pager, PR to examples repo, announce in #devexp and Monday sync

Open questions / decisions to make (triage this sprint):
- Which language bindings get first-class treatment? recommendation: node + python first, then go/rust; match top 6 languages from product telemetry
- Telemetry ingestion: do we ship a sandbox ingestion key or rely on sample ship-to endpoint? security needs clarity from infra
- Policy language: keep JSON-only for 1.0 or add a tiny DSL? JSON recommended for discoverability

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally opinionated and meant to be the smallest possible useful SDK that showcases Redwood runtime capabilities (cache, batch, fallbacks).
- Focus on reducing cognitive load for integrators: one file to read, two examples to run, and a telemetry checklist to copy into alerting stacks.

Action items (PRIORITY):
- Evan: prototype node EventEmitter and batcher (due 2024-03-22)
- Marina: draft telemetry event schema + redaction helper (due 2024-03-18)
- Samir: wire sample policy examples and update product-backed routing table (due 2024-03-20)

Appendix: helpful links and snippets
- sample policy json:
  {
    "prefer": ["hosted:fast"],
    "failover": ["hosted:small","dedicated:pool-02"],
    "qos": {"latency_ms": 250, "cost_per_1k": 0.0025}
  }
- minimal event payload example (line-delimited JSON):
  {"ts":"2024-03-12T18:00:00Z","request_id":"r123","event":"request.start","model":"gpt-like-64k","route_hint":"hosted:fast"}

Feedback welcome — please add inline comments or push to the PR linked above. This doc is a working sketch; happy to pare back further if teams prefer a single-language single-file approach first.
